What does a Forward-Deployed Engineer (FDE) do?

The video explains what a Forward-Deployed Engineer (FDE), the front-line AI engineer does. It shows why so many corporate AI projects do not generate value, the origin of the function in Palantir, how the FDE works within the client and results examples.

Published in 13 October 2026 · 8 min 34 s

  • Agentic engineering
  • Management and strategy

Open on YouTube

The video and the transcript are in Portuguese. The minutes between brackets lead to the stretch of the video.

In this article

  1. The problem: AI that does not generate value
  2. The origin: the Palantir
  3. Who is the FDE?
  4. How FDE works
  5. Results in the Real World
  6. Frequently Asked Questions

The problem: AI that does not generate value

The video uses the analogy of an investment fund: to give the most modern smartphone to the grandmother. She wants to use it, but doesn't know how to fit the device into the routine without someone next door to set up the Wi-Fi and show the apps 00:41.

With companies that buy AI the same happens: they pay dearly, but do not extract value without someone who mounts the system in place 00:41.

According to the video, a study by MIT showed that 95% of corporate AI projects do not create real value for business 01:02.

It's not the models' fault. The laboratory is a clean and controlled environment; the company has old systems, messy databases, rigid security rules and confusing processes 01:44.

The origin: the Palantir

In the 2010s, Palantir worked with government intelligence agencies, with very sensitive data. The solution was to create a team of elite engineers, the "deltas", who went to the front line to solve the problems on site 02:26.

In 2024, large AI laboratories ran into the same bottleneck. In 2026, companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic began investing billions in teams of front line engineers themselves. 02:48.

Who is the FDE?

The video compares the AI lab to the kitchen of a French restaurant focused on technique. Who guarantees that the customer leaves happy is the team of the salon: the master understands the taste of the person, manages expectations and translates everything to the chef 03:09.

In the world of technology, this role is called Forward-Deployed AI Engineer, or FDE: the front-line AI engineer 03:29.

The FDE is not just a programmer or a consultant who gives advice and leaves. He's a hybrid professional, who enters the client's company, understands the routine and puts his hand in the dough for the machine to work there. 03:51.

The traditional software engineer creates at headquarters a standardized tool for thousands of people. The FDE does the opposite: it goes to the front line and builds various tailor-made solutions for a single customer 04:12.

The goal is not the most revolutionary code, but that the tool has real use and that people trust it. 04:33.

How FDE works

The routine has four steps 04:55:

1. Sit with the client's team and live the problem, rather than evaluate from a distance 04:55. 2. Builds the solution inside, mixing new code with old company systems 04:55. 3. Apply rigorous tests to make sure the AI doesn't screw up 05:15. 4. Stays until the implementation, accompanying until people use the tool every day 05:15.

He writes real code instead of sending a PDF with suggestions 05:15.

Tools have complicated names, but simple ideas 05:35:

  • RAG: give the IA reading glasses, so she can read the company documents and emails before answering 05:35;
  • evals: quality tests to ensure that AI does not hallucinate 05:35;
  • guardrails: Protection grids, the limits for AI not doing anything dangerous or leaving company rules 05:56.

Results in the Real World

According to the video 06:17:

  • at John Deere, the FDEs went to farms and helped create an AI system that cut the use of chemicals in plantations by 70%. 06:17;
  • at BBVA bank, the work of the FDEs allowed to run the AI safely for more than 120,000 employees 06:39;
  • in call center systems, what the FDEs saw go wrong at the tip went back to the laboratories and improved the models. 06:39.

The demand for front-line engineers has increased by 800% in vacancies in the last year, with high wages, while traditional technology vacancies continue at a normal pace 07:00.

The message is that having a brilliant idea is not enough: the value is in the implementation 07:22.

The video concludes that the AI revolution depends on human empathy: people side by side with users, translating the machine so that it is safe and useful 07:44.

Frequently Asked Questions

What's the difference between an FDE and a consultant?

The consultant advises and leaves. FDE enters the client company and writes the code that makes the solution work there 03:51.

Where does the FDE function come from?

From Palantir, in the decade of 2010, with engineers called "deltas" 02:26.

Reviewed by Maurício Yokoyama Issei in 19 November 2026.

About the video

Did you know that about 95% of artificial-generative intelligence pilot projects in companies fail to generate real business value? To close the gap between advanced AI models and the operational reality of organizations, one of the most demanding functions of technology emerged: the **Forward-Deployed Engineer (FDE)**.

In this explanatory video, we detail how this hybrid professional — nicknamed "the human translator of the AI" — works directly in companies to transform prototypes into functional production systems.

**What you will learn in this video:**
• ** Origin of FDE:** As the model emerged at Palantir with Shyam Sankar and his engineers known internally as "Deltas".
• ** The Corporate IA Gargalo:** Because the market has registered a growth of over 700% in the search for FDEs in giants like OpenAI, Anthropic and Google Cloud.
• ** The Triple Competence:** As FDE unites full-stack and cloud engineering, AI workflows (such as RAG, agents and evals) and strategic business vision.
• **From Code to Result:** Why the real competitive advantage is not only in the models, but in making them work within complex corporate environments.
